title: Natural characteristic Picard sequence for a split reductive group
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $H$ a reductive $F$-group [def-sc-group-scheme]. A reductive group means a smooth affine group of finite type, geometrically connected, whose extension to an algebraic closure has no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup [def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology, def-sfb-solvable-group-structure]. A split maximal torus means a maximal torus isomorphic over the ground field to $\mathbf G_m^r$ for an integer $r\geq0$ [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type]. Assume $H$ has a split maximal torus $T$. A Borel subgroup is a smooth geometrically connected closed subgroup whose extension to an algebraic closure is maximal among smooth connected solvable closed subgroups, where solvable means having a finite normal series with commutative successive quotients [def-sfb-solvable-group-structure]. There exists a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$ such that $B=U\rtimes T$ for a split smooth connected unipotent group $U$; split here means admitting a finite series of smooth connected normal successive subgroups with quotients $\mathbf G_a$ [def-sc-gm-ga]. For every such pair, write $r_B:B\to T$ for the projection. The fppf sheaf quotient $Q=H/B$ is represented by a smooth projective geometrically integral $F$-scheme, and $f:H\to Q$ is the quotient map. The fppf quotient means sheafification of $A\mapsto H(A)/B(A)$ for faithfully flat finitely presented covers. Put $X_F^*(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_{F\text{-grp}}(T,\mathbf G_m)$, with addition given by multiplication of characters. For every scheme $Y$, $\operatorname{Pic}(Y)$ is the abelian group of isomorphism classes of invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-modules, with tensor product as addition; invertible means locally free of rank one [def-sc-invertible-module]. Pullback means tensor inverse image [def-pc-module-pullback]. Define $c_F:X_F^*(T)\to\operatorname{Pic}(Q)$ by the associated line bundle $H\times^B\mathbf A^1$, with right action $(h,z)b=(hb,\chi(r_B(b))^{-1}z)$. This is a homomorphism and $$X_F^*(T)\xrightarrow{c_F}\operatorname{Pic}(Q)\xrightarrow{f^*}\operatorname{Pic}(H)\longrightarrow0$$ is exact: $f^*$ is surjective and $\ker f^*=\operatorname{im}c_F$. For every field extension $L/F$ [def-pc-field-extension], the scalar extended pair $T_L\subseteq B_L\subseteq H_L$ has the same properties, $Q_L=H_L/B_L$, and the scalar extension maps on characters and the pullbacks on Picard groups give a commutative diagram between these two exact sequences, in particular $p_Q^*c_F(\chi)=c_L(\chi_L)$ and $p_H^*f^*M=f_L^*p_Q^*M$. Here $p_Q:Q_L\to Q$ and $p_H:H_L\to H$ are the projections [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Milne, Algebraic Groups, Theorem 18.15, sequence (128), printed p.390, and section 18.f, pp.395-396; the split-group standing assumptions, B/ B_u and characteristic line bundle on p.390. Scalar-extension compatibility of the associated-bundle construction is made explicit. Also Brion Lemma 2.3, equation (2), printed p.118.

proof.text: Fix a splitting $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$ and an algebraic closure $\bar F$. By [lem-sfb-maximal-torus-field-extension], $T_{\bar F}$ is maximal in $H_{\bar F}$. The adjoint action has finitely many weights: write its coaction as $c(v)=\sum_a v_a\otimes x^a$; comparing coefficients in coassociativity gives $c(v_a)=v_a\otimes x^a$, and the counit gives $v=\sum_a v_a$. A finite basis yields finitely many exponents and the direct sum of these weight spaces. Thus the set $\Phi$ of nontrivial adjoint weights is the root set used in [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description]. All its characters are Laurent monomials $x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_r^{a_r}$ with integral exponents, hence are already defined on $T$ over $F$. Indeed a character is a group-like Laurent polynomial: coefficient comparison in $c(xy)=c(x)c(y)$ leaves exactly one coefficient, equal to $1$. Choose integers $(b_i)$ with $\sum_i a_i b_i\ne0$ for every $\alpha=(a_i)\in\Phi$: for $r>0$ use $(1,N,\ldots,N^{r-1})$ and avoid the finitely many integer roots of these nonzero integer polynomials. For $r=0$, $\Phi$ is empty and take $\lambda=0$. This defines $\lambda(t)=(t^{b_i})$ over $F$. The cited regular-cocharacter theorem says that $(P_\lambda)_{\bar F}$ is a Borel containing $T_{\bar F}$.

source.place: Corollary 21.30, printed p.434; Proposition 21.29, pp.433-434; integral avoidance made explicit.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-reductive-cocharacter-parabolic-geometry]. It gives $Z_\lambda=T$ and $P_\lambda=U_\lambda\rtimes T$ with $U_\lambda$ split smooth connected unipotent. Step 1 identifies $(P_\lambda)_{\bar F}$ as a Borel, so $B=P_\lambda$ is a Borel over $F$ with the source's geometric definition. This proves the required existence with its specified torus. In particular, no assumption that $F$ is perfect or algebraically closed has been introduced.

source.place: Theorem 13.33 and Corollary 21.34, pp.265-266,435; geometric Borel definition in 17.66, p.375.

proof.text: Fix any pair $T\subseteq B$ in the statement. By the geometric definition of Borel, $B_{\bar F}$ is a Borel of $H_{\bar F}$ containing $T_{\bar F}$. By [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description], it is $P_\mu$ for a regular integral cocharacter $\mu$ of $T_{\bar F}$. The Laurent-coordinate description in step 1 defines the same $\mu$ over $F$. The field-extension clause in [lem-sfb-reductive-cocharacter-parabolic-geometry] and injectivity on coordinate rings identify $B=P_\mu$ over $F$: their defining ideals agree after faithfully flat tensor extension. By [lem-sfb-unipotent-to-multiplicative-trivial], $r_B$ kills $U_\mu$ and is the identity on $T$, so on $B=U_\mu\rtimes T$ it equals $r_\mu$ and its kernel is $U=U_\mu$. That node now gives $Q=H/B$ smooth projective geometrically integral, $H$ geometrically integral, and $f$ a smooth surjective finite-presentation torsor with geometrically integral fibres. Since $B=U\rtimes T$ is split solvable (append to the given additive series the inverse images of the coordinate subtori in $T$), [lem-sfb-split-solvable-torsors-and-variety] gives Zariski local sections of $f$ and $\operatorname{Pic}(B_K)=0$ for every field $K/F$. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular] makes $H,Q$ regular; they are separated and of finite type, as required for generic-line descent below.

source.place: Theorem 21.32 and Corollary 21.34, pp.434-435; Theorem 18.15 proof, final paragraph p.396; Proposition 16.55(c) and Corollary 16.56, p.344.

proof.text: The torsor identity identifies its double overlap with $H\times_F B$. On the trivial line put the descent action $(h,z)b=(hb,\chi(r_B(b))^{-1}z)$. The character identity gives the cocycle on triple overlaps. The map $f$ is an fpqc cover (flat, surjective and quasi-compact), so [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] produces the invertible module $L_\chi$ on $Q$ with this descent datum. Multiplication of line coordinates identifies $L_\chi\otimes L_\psi$ with $L_{\chi+\psi}$: on overlaps the transition multipliers multiply. The zero character has multiplier $1$ and descends to $\mathcal O_Q$. Thus $c_F$ is a homomorphism. Its pullback has the global frame $h\mapsto[h,1]$, so $\operatorname{im}c_F\subseteq\ker f^*$.

source.place: Section 18.c, printed p.390; Stacks descent.tex Tag 023T, proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent.

proof.text: We need a product-unit identity over $F$, not just over an algebraically closed field. If $a:H\times_F B\to\mathbf G_m$ is a unit, base change it to $\bar F$. Both factors there are integral separated finite-type schemes by step 3. Apply the displayed normalized identity of [lem-sfb-rosenlicht-product-unit-factorization] at the rational points $(1,1)$. It gives $a(h,b)=a(h,1)a(1,b)a(1,1)^{-1}$ after extension to $\bar F$. All four functions are defined over $F$. Their equality already holds in $F[H]\otimes_FF[B]$: its map to its tensor product with $\bar F$ is injective, as is seen by extending any nonzero vector to an $F$-basis. This proves the same identity over $F$ on every test algebra.

source.place: Theorem 18.32, pp.395-396, using Remark 12.50 and Proposition 12.48, pp.246-247; rational-point scalar descent supplied explicitly.

proof.text: Every character $\eta:B\to\mathbf G_m$ is trivial on $U$ by [lem-sfb-unipotent-to-multiplicative-trivial]. In the product $B=U\rtimes T$, write $b=ut$; then $\eta(b)=\eta(u)\eta(t)=\eta(t)$. Hence restriction and composition with $r_B$ give inverse isomorphisms $X_F^*(B)\simeq X_F^*(T)$. In particular the same associated line construction for characters of $B$ is exactly $c_F$, with the sign convention in the question.

Let $M$ be an invertible module on $Q$ for which $f^*M$ is trivial, and choose its global frame $s$. Over $H\times_F B$, the frames $s(hb)$ and $s(h)$ are in the same pulled-back line, so $s(hb)=s(h)a(h,b)$ for a regular unit $a$, with $a(h,1)=1$. Step 5 gives $a(h,b)=a(1,b)$. Associativity applied twice to the frame gives $a(1,b_1b_2)=a(1,b_1)a(1,b_2)$ as an identity of regular functions, so $\eta(b)=a(1,b)$ is a character. Step 6 writes it as $\chi\circ r_B$. Now $(h,z)\mapsto s(h)z$ is invariant for $(h,z)b=(hb,\eta(b)^{-1}z)$, since $s(hb)\eta(b)^{-1}z=s(h)z$. Full faithfulness of [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] descends this map and its inverse to $L_\chi\simeq M$. This proves $\ker f^*\subseteq\operatorname{im}c_F$, and step 4 gives the other inclusion.

source.place: Theorem 18.32, exactness at Pic(X), printed pp.395-396.

proof.text: For an invertible module $N$ on $H$, let $K=F(Q)$ and $\xi=\operatorname{Spec}K$. A Zariski section of $f$ on a nonempty open of the integral scheme $Q$ identifies $H_\xi$ with $B_K$. Thus $N|_{H_\xi}$ is trivial by [lem-sfb-split-solvable-torsors-and-variety]. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-generic-trivial-line-descent] to $f:H\to Q$. Step 3 verifies both schemes regular integral separated finite type, and the morphism smooth surjective with nonempty geometrically integral fibres. The conclusion supplies an invertible module $M$ on $Q$ with $f^*M\simeq N$. Therefore $f^*$ is surjective. Together with steps 4 and 7 this is exactly the asserted right-exact characteristic sequence.

source.place: Theorem 18.32, omitted exactness at Pic(Y), and Corollary 16.56, pp.396,344; generic vertical-divisor form supplied by the cited node (Stacks Tags 00ON, 0AGA, 0AG0).

proof.text: Let $L/F$ be any field extension. With $\mu$ as in step 3, [lem-sfb-reductive-cocharacter-parabolic-geometry] identifies $B_L=(P_\mu)_L=P_{\mu_L}$ and $Q_L=H_L/B_L$, with the pulled-back quotient projection. Define $r_{B_L}=(r_B)_L$; tensoring the given semidirect-product isomorphism makes it the projection $B_L=U_L\rtimes T_L\to T_L$. The torus $T_L$ is split by scalar extending $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$. Since $U=U_\mu$ by step 3, the cocharacter-parabolic node identifies $U_L=U_{\mu_L}$ and states that this group is split unipotent over $L$. By [lem-sfb-maximal-torus-field-extension], $T_L$ is maximal. Regularity of $\mu$ is unchanged because its integer pairings are unchanged, so [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description] over an algebraic closure of $L$ makes $B_L$ a Borel. The cocharacter-parabolic node gives the quotient's geometric properties over $L$. Thus steps 4-8 apply over $L$, giving the second exact sequence.

source.place: Theorem 17.82, p.379; cocharacter functors of Theorem 13.33 and Corollary 21.34, pp.265-266,435; scalar extension of the quotient.

proof.text: Finally take a Zariski cover $\{V_i\}$ of $Q$ with sections $\sigma_i:V_i\to H$. Write $\sigma_j=\sigma_i b_{ij}$ on overlaps; the group element $b_{ij}$ exists uniquely by the torsor identity. The relation $[\sigma_j,z]=[\sigma_i,\chi(r_B(b_{ij}))z]$ shows that these are the transition factors of $L_\chi$. After tensoring with $L$, the very same formulas with $(b_{ij})_L$ are the transition factors defining $L_{\chi_L}$ over $Q_L$, because $r_{B_L}=(r_B)_L$. Thus [lem-pc-fpqc-descent], applied to this Zariski cover, identifies $p_Q^*L_\chi\simeq L_{\chi_L}$. This proves $p_Q^*c_F(\chi)=c_L(\chi_L)$ with the specified sign. The quotient square satisfies $f\circ p_H=p_Q\circ f_L$. On local modules, tensor associativity sends $(m\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $m\otimes ab$ and identifies pullback along a composite with successive tensor pullbacks. It therefore identifies $p_H^*f^*M$ and $f_L^*p_Q^*M$. Pullback also respects tensor product by the same map, so the vertical Picard maps are homomorphisms. Both squares of the claimed diagram now commute.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q92-3ba624deb (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the 10-step split in full, both new unsplit statement-only nodes, every cited statement, and Milne 13.33, 17.60, 17.82, 18.14-18.15 (p.390) and 25.1 in the PDF. Steps 1-3: maximal-torus-field-extension, then a regular integral cocharacter chosen by avoiding finitely many integer hyperplanes, then regular-cocharacter-borel-description over F-bar. This gives B=P_lambda=U rtimes T with U split. For any Borel containing T, the cocharacter mu is defined over F because T is split, equality descends faithfully flat, and r_B=r_mu by unipotent-to-multiplicative-trivial. Steps 4 and 7: descent cocycle and sign checked, s(hb)eta(b)^-1 z = s(h)z, matching Milne's action. Step 5: Rosenlicht over F-bar descended by tensor injectivity. Step 8: the hypotheses of split-solvable Pic(B_K)=0 and of generic-line descent are verified (regular, integral, separated, finite type; fibres geometrically integral). Steps 9-10: base change and transition factors chi(r_B(b_ij)). New nodes are true and not duplicates: maximal-torus-field-extension is Milne 17.82, valid for any group variety; cocharacter-parabolic-geometry is 13.33 + 17.60 + 25.1 + the regular centralizer, and it is the only general-field cocharacter node in the DAG.
